## 1. Learning objectives
After this lesson you can:
- write a subclass with `extends` and explain what it gets for free;
- call the parent's constructor with `super(...)` and the parent's method with `super.method()`;
- **override** a method and use `@Override` so the compiler checks you;
- explain why a `Person` variable can hold a `Customer` object, and which `describe()` then runs;
- apply the **IS-A test**: "a customer IS-A person" is true, "a sale IS-A customer" is not.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- Lesson 11's `Customer` had a name and a phone. Now the shop also needs **staff** (cashiers and managers), and they
  have a name and a phone too. Copy and paste would make two places to fix every bug.
- **Inheritance** lets a class build on another. `Customer extends Person` means "a `Customer` is a `Person` with extra
  things". `Person` is the **parent** (superclass); `Customer` and `Staff` are **children** (subclasses).
- A child gets the parent's public methods for free: `ana.getName()` works although `Customer` never wrote it.
- **`super(name, phone)`** runs the parent's constructor, and must be the first line of the child's constructor.
  **`super.label()`** calls the parent's version of a method from inside the child.
- **Overriding.** A child may replace a parent's method with the same name and parameters. `Person.describe()` returns
  the name; `Staff.describe()` returns `"Mara Cruz (cashier)"`. Always write **`@Override`** above it: if you misspell
  the name, the compiler complains instead of silently creating a different method.
- **Which version runs?** The one that matches the **object**, not the variable. If `Person p = new Staff(...)`,
  `p.describe()` runs the `Staff` version. This is the first taste of **polymorphism** ("many shapes"); lesson 14 builds on it.
- `Person.toString()` simply returns `describe()`. So printing any person prints it in its own way, and `Customer`
  and `Staff` did not have to write `toString` at all.
- **`private` fields stay private** even from children. `Staff` cannot say `name`; it calls `getName()`.
- **IS-A or HAS-A?** Use inheritance only for IS-A. A `Sale` *has a* `Customer` (lesson 11), it is not one.
  Overusing inheritance makes code hard to change; when in doubt, prefer HAS-A (composition).
- **Intentional refactor.** `name`, `phone`, `getName()` and `getPhone()` **move** from `Customer` to `Person`.
  `Customer`'s own `toString()` becomes `describe()`. The output for customers is unchanged, so `CustomerTest` passes untouched.
- **Honest limits.** `Staff` is not used by the menu yet (logins arrive in the security week), and the role is still a `String`
  that could be misspelled. Lesson 15 replaces it with an enum.

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/InheritanceDemo.java` — `Item` and `Perishable extends Item`, with `super`, `@Override` and `instanceof`.
```
java lessons/13-inheritance/examples/InheritanceDemo.java
```
```java
class Perishable extends Item {
    Perishable(String name, int daysLeft) {
        super(name);               // build the Item part first
        this.daysLeft = daysLeft;
    }
    @Override
    String label() {
        return super.label() + " (expires in " + daysLeft + " days)";   // reuse the parent version
    }
}
```

## 5. Practical exercises
In `exercises/` (`Employee.java`, `Manager.java`, tests in `Exercises13Test.java`):
1. `Employee` — name and a monthly pay in centavos: `monthlyPay()`, `annualPay()` (12 x `monthlyPay()`), `describe()`.
2. `Manager extends Employee` — adds a bonus: override `monthlyPay()` using `super.monthlyPay()`.
   Notice that `annualPay()` and `describe()` need no change: they call `monthlyPay()`, so they pick up the bonus.

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `constructor Person in class Person cannot be applied to given types` | The child constructor has no `super(...)` call, and `Person` has no no-argument constructor | Add `super(name, phone);` as the first line |
| `call to super must be first statement in constructor` | `super(...)` is not the first line | Move it to the top |
| `name has private access in Person` | A child used the parent's private field | Call `getName()` |
| `method does not override or implement a method from a supertype` | `@Override` on a misspelled or different-signature method | Match the parent's name and parameters exactly |
| The parent's version runs instead of the child's | The method is not overridden (different parameters) or is `static` | Same name, same parameters, not static |
| `Person p = ...; p.getRole()` does not compile | The *variable* type decides what you may call | Cast, `((Staff) p).getRole()`, or hold it in a `Staff` variable |
| Output of a customer changed | `describe()` text differs from the old `toString` | Match `Ana Reyes (12 points)` exactly |
